adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Admin::EmbeddingController builds a synthetic OpenStruct in `fetch_embedding` with `id: 'default'` and `embeddable_hosts`, and its `update` action only re-renders the same serialized object (no persistence or mutations) (app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:16-21). On the client, `admin-embedding` controller defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({});` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:6-8), but the new template `embedding.hbs` contains no UI element invoking `saveChanges`, only `addHost`/`deleteHost`. So the finding that the endpoint/update action exist primarily to satisfy a single-record Ember-store shape and that `saveChanges` has no server effect / is effectively dead is grounded, but it’s more of a scope/architecture/unnecessary-code concern than a functional defect.
